title: A Salt for the Hollow Again
premise: August Vane has kept the Hollow Gate sealed for twenty years, hiding her magic behind a charm-seller's stall in the city of Corren, where magic is outlawed. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, she learns her long-lost brother's soul was sold to the court beneath Mount Sere as payment for the gate's original binding—and the usurper Malachai Voss intends to reopen the gate using that soul as a key. August joins a smuggler crew, a disgraced warder, and a half-fae archivist to steal the soul back, discovering along the way that her own keeping of the gate was itself an act of complicity in Voss's rise. In the end, August must choose between sealing the gate forever at the cost of her brother's soul or shattering it and letting magic return to the world; she shatters it, frees her brother, and builds a new found family amid the ruins of her old secrecy.
about_author: Bram Montrose is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping coastal trade routes before turning to fantasy fiction. They live in a drafty house full of tide charts, half-finished maps, and one extremely judgmental cat.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: POV: August. In outlawed-magic Corren, August sells harmless charms by day and secretly maintains the Hollow Gate's wards by night. A routine inspection nearly exposes her when a warder lingers over her stall. The chapter establishes her careful invisibility and ends with the first tremor in the wards—a hairline crack no one else notices.

chapters.title: Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: POV: August. The stars go out all at once, and the border wards fall with them. Panic spreads through Corren as refugees arrive claiming the northern sky is 'peeling.' August realizes only someone with gate-knowledge could have unmade the wards. She packs her tools, torn between fleeing and investigating, and chooses investigation—her first break from twenty years of stillness.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: August. At the Hollow Gate, August finds the binding sigils rewritten in blood-ink—someone has been feeding the gate a soul's essence for years. The residual signature is achingly familiar: her brother Tomas, lost at fourteen. Grief and guilt collide as she understands her 'keeping' masked a theft. Emotional beat: devastation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: POV: August. To reach Mount Sere, August bargains passage with Wren Calloway, captain of the salt-smuggler Kestrel, paying with a forbidden luck-charm. Wren tests her ruthlessly before accepting. The crew—skeptical, sharp-edged, alive—gives August her first taste of belonging in decades. Beat: wary connection kindled under mutual distrust.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash Roads
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Through Wren's eyes we see August's competence and her lies. The Kestrel runs a burned checkpoint where Voss's soldiers interrogate travelers about 'a woman who keeps gates.' Wren covers for August without knowing why, then demands the truth. August gives a partial truth—the soul, not the gate. Beat: loyalty beginning to outweigh suspicion.

chapters.title: The Archivist Below
chapters.summary: POV: August. In the free city of Dellamere, they recruit Ilex, a half-fae archivist exiled for cataloguing forbidden gate-lore. Ilex confirms the court beneath Mount Sere buys souls as currency and reveals Voss was once a gate-warder himself—August's former mentor. Beat: the past becomes personal; the enemy gains a face.

chapters.title: Lessons in Ruin
chapters.summary: POV: August (flashback interwoven). Flashbacks show young August apprenticed to Voss, learning ward-craft and absorbing his doctrine that control justifies anything. Present-day August recognizes how his teachings shaped her own secrecy. Ilex warns that gates don't imprison power—they concentrate it. Beat: dawning horror at her own complicity.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Summons
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Inside Mount Sere's approach, Voss prepares the ritual to reopen the Hollow Gate, needing only the final resonance of Tomas's soul. He senses August's interference like a familiar itch. His chapters reveal genuine conviction—he believes reopening the gate will save the world from slow magical decay. Beat: chilling sympathy for the antagonist.

chapters.title: Crossing the Gray Marches
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. The Kestrel crew crosses a blighted marsh where fallen wards have let wild magic fester. A crew member, Fen, is injured by a feral spell; August saves him openly, revealing her magic to the whole crew. Instead of betrayal, they close ranks around her. Beat: found family solidifying through shared risk.

chapters.title: A Debt in Bone
chapters.summary: POV: August. At a waystation, August meets a bone-oracle who shows her a vision: if the gate reopens, Voss will bind every living mage to it—including her. But sealing it forever means Tomas's soul is consumed as fuel. The oracle offers a third path hinted in a riddle: 'a gate dies when its keeper stops being one.' Beat: hope with a terrible price tag.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: POV: August. The crew infiltrates Mount Sere through Ilex's archived servant-tunnels. The subterranean court is gilded horror—fae nobility trading souls like coin. August locates Tomas's soul-vessel but triggers a ward keyed to her own bloodline. Alarms rise. Beat: awe curdling to panic; the heist begins to unravel.

chapters.title: Brother, Unbound
chapters.summary: POV: August. Cornered, August reaches the vessel and speaks to what remains of Tomas—not a boy but a compressed constellation of memory. He recognizes her and, heartbreakingly, forgives her absence. She can't extract him without collapsing the vault. Wren arrives to cover her retreat. Beat: love and impossibility intertwined.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Gilded Dark
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. One crew member, Harl, sells their location to the court to buy his sister's freedom. The escape becomes a running battle through the tunnels; Ilex is captured buying the others time. Wren must choose between retrieving Ilex and getting August out. She chooses August—and hates herself for it. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: What We Buried at Dellamere
chapters.summary: POV: August. Regrouping in hiding, the fractured crew confronts Harl. August refuses to execute him, arguing that Voss's world makes traitors of everyone. The argument splits the group until Wren backs August—not because she agrees, but because mercy is the thing worth building. Beat: the found family fractures and re-forms on new terms.

chapters.title: The Warder's Confession
chapters.summary: POV: August. Ilex escapes captivity and delivers a stolen ledger proving August's twenty years of quiet ward-work unknowingly siphoned stray magic toward Voss's ritual—her invisibility fed him. August breaks down; Wren holds the pieces together. Beat: rock bottom, and the first honest reckoning with her own corruption-by-caution.

chapters.title: Armies on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Voss's armies march on the free cities, and refugees flood the coast. The Kestrel evacuates civilians while August works desperately on the riddle's answer: a keeper ceases to be one by giving the gate away—by distributing its binding among many willing hands. Beat: purpose crystallizing from despair.

chapters.title: The Many-Handed Seal
chapters.summary: POV: August. August teaches fragments of ward-craft to volunteers—fishwives, soldiers, children—breaking the law and her own isolation in one stroke. Each person takes a thread of the gate's binding. It's messy, imperfect, human. Voss's scouts report the gate 'flickering.' Beat: power dispersed is power protected; the theme made action.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Hollow
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Voss assaults the Hollow Gate with his army, furious that the binding now lives in hundreds of minds he cannot cut out. His POV cracks—his conviction fraying into obsession. August stands on the wall, publicly revealed as a mage, and offers him surrender. He refuses. Beat: the moral climax staged before the physical one.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Gate
chapters.summary: POV: August. In the battle's heart, August chooses the third path: she shatters the gate entirely, releasing Tomas's soul to finally die free and pouring the gate's stored power back into the land. Magic returns to the world—wild, ungovernable, everywhere. Voss, reaching for the collapsing gate, is unmade by the power he sought to own. Beat: cathartic, costly climax.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. The stars return. Cities reckon with magic's return—fear, wonder, reprisals. Wren surveys her battered crew: Fen mending, Harl forgiven but not forgotten, Ilex drafting new laws for a world with open skies. August is missing from the count. Beat: grief braided with tentative joy.

chapters.title: Where Keepers Go
chapters.summary: POV: August. August survived, drained near death, and walks home along the salt road anonymously for the last time. She visits Tomas's grave and leaves the broken vessel there. In Corren, she reopens her charm stall—but now teaches ward-craft openly in the evenings. Beat: quiet reconciliation with the self she used to hide.

chapters.title: A Salt for the Hollow Again
chapters.summary: POV: August (closing ensemble). One year later: the Kestrel crew gathers at the rebuilt Hollow crossing—no gate now, just an open road marked by a standing stone. August salts the threshold in old tradition, welcoming rather than barring. Wren proposes a voyage north; Ilex has maps; the family says yes. Final beat: the hollow filled, not by power, but by people.
